steps.title: Permit
steps.body: At 16 you can get a special learner's permit by enrolling in an approved behind-the-wheel course with a parent's consent. Otherwise, you can get an examination permit at 17.
steps.tip: We handle the enrollment paperwork with you.

steps.title: Written test
steps.body: Pass the knowledge test (50 questions, 40 correct) and a vision test at the MVC.
steps.tip: We review signs, rules and practice questions with you.

steps.title: Behind-the-wheel lessons
steps.body: Complete 6 hours of instruction in a dual-controlled car with a licensed instructor, then keep practicing.
steps.tip: Lessons go at your pace, in your language.

steps.title: Road test
steps.body: Show the examiner you can drive safely. You're encouraged to practice with, and test in, our school car.
steps.tip: Didn't pass? You can retest after 14 days.

steps.title: Your license
steps.body: You'll start with a probationary license. After a year of unsupervised driving, you can move to a basic license.

guide.title: How to get your driver's license in New Jersey
guide.intro: A plain-language walkthrough of New Jersey's Graduated Driver License (GDL) program, from your first permit to your basic license.
guide.helpTitle: Want help with any of these steps?
guide.helpBody: We help students through the whole process, in Spanish or English.

sections.title: How the NJ license process works
paragraphs: New Jersey licenses new drivers in stages through its Graduated Driver License (GDL) program. You start with a permit, practice with supervision, pass a road test, drive with a probationary license, and then earn your basic license.
bullets: Probationary license → basic license after 1 year

sections.title: Step 1: Get your permit
paragraphs: There are two common paths, depending on your age.
bullets: Age 16: a special learner's permit, if you're enrolled in an approved behind-the-wheel course with a licensed driving school and have parental consent. You must pass the knowledge and vision tests.
Age 17 and up: teens who don't take the course wait until 17 for an examination permit.

sections.title: Step 2: The knowledge and vision tests
paragraphs: The knowledge test has 50 questions. You need 40 correct answers to pass. You'll also take a vision test.
Study the official NJ Driver Manual and check the MVC's identification requirements (the 6 Points of ID) before you go.
bullets: Vision test at the same visit

sections.title: Step 3: Behind-the-wheel instruction
paragraphs: The special learner's permit path includes 6 hours of behind-the-wheel instruction in a dual-controlled vehicle with a licensed instructor. Many students take extra lessons to feel fully ready.

sections.title: Step 4: Supervised driving
paragraphs: Before the road test, you'll practice with a supervising driver.
bullets: Under 21: 6 months of supervised driving. New rules also call for 50 hours of supervised practice.
21 and older: a shorter period of 3 months.

sections.title: Step 5: The road test
paragraphs: The road test checks that you can drive safely and handle common maneuvers. Students are encouraged to practice with, and test in, the school's car so everything feels familiar.
If you don't pass, you can retest after 14 days. Use that time to practice the parts that gave you trouble.

sections.title: Step 6: Probationary and basic license
paragraphs: After you pass, you receive a probationary license. After 1 year of unsupervised driving, you can move up to a basic license.

sections.title: GDL restrictions for young drivers
paragraphs: Young drivers have extra rules while they hold a permit or probationary license. For example, with a special learner's permit you can't drive between 11:01 PM and 5:00 AM.
Other GDL rules may apply. Check the MVC for the complete, current list.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: Clear answers about permits, lessons and the road test in New Jersey. Still unsure? Call or message us.

items.a: Yes. We teach in Spanish and English, and our team also speaks Portuguese and Arabic. Tell us your preferred language when you book.

items.q: I'm very nervous about driving. Can you help?
items.a: Absolutely. We specialize in first-time and nervous drivers. We start on quiet streets, explain each step before trying it, and move at your pace.

items.q: How old do I need to be to get a permit in NJ?
items.a: At 16 you can get a special learner's permit if you're enrolled in an approved behind-the-wheel course with parental consent and you pass the knowledge and vision tests. Teens who don't take the course wait until 17 for an examination permit.

items.q: How many hours of behind-the-wheel training are required?
items.a: The special learner's permit path includes 6 hours of behind-the-wheel instruction in a dual-controlled car with a licensed instructor. You can always add more lessons if you want extra practice.

items.q: How many questions are on the NJ knowledge test?
items.a: 50 questions. You need 40 correct answers to pass. You'll also take a vision test.

items.q: How long do I have to practice before the road test?
items.a: If you're under 21, plan on 6 months of supervised driving, and new rules also call for 50 hours of supervised practice. If you're 21 or older, the period is shorter: 3 months.

items.q: Can I use your car for the road test?
items.a: Yes. Students are encouraged to practice with our school car and use it for the road test, so everything feels familiar. Call us to plan it.

items.q: What happens if I fail the road test?
items.a: It happens, and it's okay. You can retest after 14 days. We'll focus your next lessons on what gave you trouble.

items.q: Are there restrictions for new young drivers?
items.a: Yes. New Jersey's GDL rules apply. For example, with a special learner's permit you can't drive between 11:01 PM and 5:00 AM. Check nj.gov/mvc for the full, current list.
You'll get a probationary license. After 1 year of unsupervised driving, you can move up to a basic license.
Our lessons are affordable, and prices depend on the program. Call us for current rates and packages.
